gap_reasons: The delivered result characterizes efficiency and proves uniform attainment for binary treatment, one binary missing confounder, and ternary outcomes on the declared strictly feasible locus; it does not settle the restricted-tangent problem throughout the Wen–McGee model

The joint-profile ball forces nonsingularity of [d_0 d_1], excluding positive compatible laws with collinear treatment-profile directions even when the four observable normals remain independent, so the singular-strata extension earns no credit

The four determinant restrictions specialize equalities already stated in [Sjölander–Hägg, Section 6, equation (8)](https://academic.oup.com/biomet/article/112/2/asaf009/8006713), making tangent completeness and efficient attainment the contribution rather than discovery of those restrictions

The consumer prose asserting the same published opioid-mortality estimand overclaims: [Wen–McGee’s application](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.21786) estimates observed mortality risk minus risk under no opioids and includes multiple missing confounders, whereas this theorem concerns the treatment-versus-control risk difference with one binary missing confounder

Independent reconstruction confirms the witness cells, four normals, covariance matrix, and bound 1.8010491644, but the supporting evidence establishes precision gain for a constructed table and its neighborhood, not its magnitude or feasibility in NHANES

proof_attempt_summary: The final discovery math and rubric panels passed the regular-locus tangent characterization, canonical-gradient projection, strict-gain witness and uniform efficient attainment. Four inaccessible textbook facts were replaced by independently reviewed Lean-backed proofs, with explicit positive-sample and root conventions and a nonempty-class coverage qualifier. The field claim did not survive the final scope/application assessment: singular strata remain open, the consumer framing overstates the application match, and full Lean formalization/F5 acceptance was not completed in this round.
tldr: In the ambient cause-resolved Wen--McGee model \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{WM}}^{\mathrm{cause}}\), outcome independence for ternary mortality imposes four observable mixture equalities almost everywhere. The law-invariant class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sf}}(\eta,\gamma)\) supplies regular base points and compact uniformity, with coordinatewise Fr\'echet operator-norm H\"older smoothness and the \(C^{s-1,1}\) convention at integer \(s\). Its two-sided score lift and exhaustive tangent yield a finite conditional projection and an observable necessary-and-sufficient strict-gain criterion. The causal witness has effect \(7/20\), with exact bounds \(351432650123351101/195126627894082560\) and \(2087/1040\), approximately \(1.8010491644\) and \(2.0067307692\). A residual-corrected estimator attains the bound with uniform studentized inference for every qualifying cross-fitted learner; a deterministic ordered entropy-bounded Brier-net learner realizes the required rate without a covariate-density assumption. Each fit accepts the sample size and evaluation fold and uses only its training complement among the first \(n\) observations. Cause-level outcome independence is stronger than independence for the binary death indicator; the result does not transfer to the published binary-only response model. Singular latent rank strata remain open.
gap: WenMcGee2026 identifies the all-cause effect and gives the nonparametric influence function in equation (3), but its specified Discussion paragraph leaves projection onto the restricted tangent open. Existing compatibility results do not prove a two-sided lift for the joint-missing four-pattern experiment.
fill: The paper defines the law-invariant class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sf}}(\eta,\gamma)\), proves its \(P_X\)-almost-everywhere primitive margins yield a two-sided lift and the entire four-normal tangent, projects the published gradient as a corollary, characterizes and witnesses strict gain, and attains the bound with a cross-fitted one-step estimator that subtracts the projected normal score and corrects the fitted restriction residual.
